subject: LOD Threshhold for small scale association study

messages.author: e62053773e6cd310
messages.subject: LOD Threshhold for small scale association study
parts:
So i'm currently doing a really small scale association study on a single pleiotropic locus with only 11 Markers. I would like to know which LOD threshold to choose since most functions seem to be tailored towards a whole genome or a much larger scale study. I am using 26 traits and would like to account for FDR.
Is there a way to get a p-value for a certain trait at each marker that accounts for FDR, telling me if the association at this marker is significant?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LOD Threshhold for small scale association study
parts:
With 11 markers in a single region and 26 traits, I personally wouldn't use FDR but rather seek to control the family-wise error rate.

FDR controls the proportion of discoveries that are false. To me, this is useful only when there are a lot of discoveries...on the order of 100.

R/qtl is specifically for QTL analysis in crosses rather than association generally, so I'm not sure whether it's appropriate for your situation. But I'd use scanone() to perform a permutation test, with all 26 phenotypes. Then in summary.scanoneperm(), there's an argument "controlAcrossCol" for having obtaining significance thresholds that control for the scan across phenotypes as well as the scan across the genome (or across the single locus, in your case).

The method is described in Burrage et al. (2010) (see right column on page 118) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/20127486

karl
